version: synthetic report v2 with explicit correction
metadata_label: independent completion improved (catalogue label, not a finding)

segments.text: Eight service centres were randomly assigned to offer a staff-assisted online appointment or printed instructions. The trial enrolled 320 applicants aged 60 or above. Its outcome was first application submission within seven days.
The corrected centre-adjusted difference in seven-day submission was 4 percentage points in favour of assistance (95% confidence interval: -2 to 10 percentage points).
The trial did not measure benefit receipt or later independent portal use. Its estimate concerns initial submission, not lasting independent ability.
Assisted digital access means that another person helps someone complete an online procedure. Assistance may enable task completion without demonstrating that the applicant can repeat the task alone.

correction_notice: This corrected report replaces the v1 Results estimate, which used an incorrect centre-adjustment weight. The same eight-centre study, 320 participants, outcome and follow-up window remain. Methods, Limitations and Terminology note are unchanged. It replaces v1 Results including that estimate in the companion brief.
